_comment: Effect definitions - what a verb, a world law, a designed body or the live operator can do to a body over time. An effect is a NAMED BUNDLE OF OPERATIONS with a target, a duration in rounds, a stacking policy and a revert policy. Keyed by effect id, which is what `applyEffect` consequences, the `apply_effect` operator verb and an agent body's `inbornEffects` all name. OPERATION IDS ARE A CLOSED SET (shared/EffectVocabulary.js): an entry names operations by id and each id runs the executor that already exists in src/controllers/consequences/, so a mutation keeps exactly one implementation and a mod stays a data-only package. Code, expressions and condition trees are not expressible here by design. OP PARAMETERS ARE LITERAL - `value` is a finite number, never a `:Physical.strength` placeholder: a placeholder resolves against the ACTING entity of an action in flight, and an effect applied by the operator or a world law has none, so an effect that carried one would quietly mean a different thing per caller. `operations` run once at application; `perRound` runs at the START of each later round the effect is alive (never in the round that applied it). `durationRounds` is counted from the round of application: applied at round 7 with 3 -> expiresRound 10, first perRound at round 8; 0 or absent means it lives until something removes it. `stacking` is refresh (default: re-applied at full strength, expiry pushed out, no stacking) | independent | strongest | capped (needs maxStacks). `revert` is auto (default: each reversible operation is undone by its own contribution - never an absolute write, so two live effects on one stat commute) | none. Operations absent from REVERSIBLE_EFFECT_OPERATIONS are record-only on expiry: the effect ends and the world keeps what happened, because undoing damage is healing nobody asked for. `target` is entity (default: each component of that entity carrying the field the operation names) | component. A malformed entry disables THAT entry with a warning and the rest of the file loads; an entry naming an operation this server does not know is disabled the same way, with the id in the warning - a data typo is never a crash vector. (An operation that PASSES this validation and then reaches the engine with no adapter is our bug and throws.) The three entries below are the enforcement arm of vocabulary the repository already declared: shared/StatVocabulary.js names the conditions `burning` and `corroded` and promises they deal matter loss over time, and nothing ticked them until this file did.
